messages.snippet: Dear Mr Osei, We act for Ferncliffe Alloys Limited. Our formal response to your letter before claim
messages.subject: Halstead Aerospace / Ferncliffe Alloys — response to letter before claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Mr Osei,

We act for Ferncliffe Alloys Limited. Our formal response to your letter before claim follows by post and email today. In short, liability is denied: the heats were released against mill certificates confirming AMS 4928 conformity, alpha-case can be introduced by post-delivery processing, and your client accepted the material and did not reject within the contractual 30-day window. Quantum is not admitted and is said to be excessive and in part too remote.

That said, our client is willing to attend a without-prejudice meeting and to consider a joint examination of retained samples.

Yours faithfully,
Jonathan Vane
Partner | Castle & Vane LLP

messages.subject: FW: Halstead Aerospace / Ferncliffe Alloys — response to letter before claim
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah, Robert,

Ferncliffe's denial is in (below). Three defences: (1) certs show conformity at release; (2) alpha-case from our processing; (3) deemed acceptance under clause 12 because we didn't reject within 30 days. None is strong on the metallurgy, and the 30-day point fails because the defects were latent. The openness to a joint sample exam actually plays to us. I'll put a strategy note together.

James

James Osei
Senior Associate | Whitfield Carter LLP
T +44 (0)20 7946 0034
